after.name: c. 3000 BC: Cities such as Uruk existed in southern Mesopotamia

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: Southern Mesopotamian urban centers emerged in the fourth millennium BCE; the old entry implied cities were established in exactly 3000 BCE. The Met identifies Uruk as a city around 3200 BCE and says it continued to expand after 3000. This is a regional context note, not an exact founding or a political incident. The point and 100 km radius are gameplay references, not the boundary of Sumer.
r2SourceEvidence.date_precision: Approximately 3000 BCE is a reference slot, not a founding year.
r2SourceEvidence.location_precision: Regional reference in southern Mesopotamia, not an exact site or boundary.

record.name: c. 3000 BC: Oued Beht in Morocco has evidence of Neolithic farming

r2SourceEvidence.review_note: Radiocarbon dates from surveyed pits are approximately 3400–2900 BCE; archaeological evidence includes domesticated crops and animals. The research does not prove exact continuous occupation in 3000 BCE, a precisely dated founding, or a specific community structure. A possible defensive structure dates to the second millennium BCE and is not asserted here. The coordinate is a survey reference point and the radius is a gameplay setting, not an archaeological boundary. An existing dated site record is separate from this historical event note.
r2SourceEvidence.date_precision: The archaeological date range spans centuries; this single-year slot is an approximate reference, not an exact year.
r2SourceEvidence.location_precision: Survey center; 20 km is a gameplay radius, not the site boundary.
